item.title: AI risks, Reserve Bank of India nudge spur a cybersecurity talent rush
item.description: RBI steps up cybersecurity scrutiny, prompting financial institutions to hire CISOs amid rising cyber threats and a shortage of skilled professionals ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda, Ajinkya Kawale
item.content:encoded: Regulated financial entities, including payment aggregators, are likely to step up hiring of chief information security officers (CISOs) as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sharpens its scrutiny of cybersecurity preparedness amid rising attacks and growing threats from artificial intelligence (AI).

item.title: Uber pilots Connected Journeys in Delhi, eyes pan-India rollout in 2027
item.description: The feature integrates metro travel with bikes, autos and cabs through a single journey plan on the Uber app, with a phased nationwide rollout planned by early next year.
item.dc:creator: Udisha Srivastav
item.content:encoded: Ride-hailing platform Uber is piloting its ‘Connected Journeys’ feature in Delhi, allowing commuters to combine metro travel with first- and last-mile options such as three-wheelers and two-wheelers through a single journey plan on its app. The company plans to expand the feature across India by early next year. The feature brings different modes of transport together, enabling riders to view route options, estimated travel times and fares across various legs of their journey and book the relevant services within the Uber app. Using customer and trip data, the platform will also suggest whether a bike, auto-rickshaw or cab would be a suitable option for the first or last mile, depending on the journey. However, riders will have the flexibility to manually switch between the available modes. The pilot is currently underway in Delhi, with a wider rollout planned in phases. Uber already enables metro ticket bookings through its app in several cities. Connected Journeys is part of Uber’s broader push towards integrated, multimodal mobility, as urban commuters increasingly look to combine public transport with app-based services to navigate congested cities. Commenting on the initiative, Aditya Kapoor, director of supply operations at Uber India & South Asia, said, “Connected Journeys is one way we can help bring those modes together, making it easier for riders to combine Metro with Uber for the first and last mile and complete their journeys more seamlessly.”

item.title: COP31 climate talks expose deep divides over fossil fuels and finance
item.description: COP31's failure to reach a political agreement exposes deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, putting global climate goals further at risk ...
item.dc:creator: Business Standard Editorial Comment
item.content:encoded: No one was surprised when the 31st Conference of Parties (COP31) summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended without a central political agreement — the Antalya Pacts — despite running into two days of overtime. If anything, the longest-running climate talks in United Nations history highlighted the festering divisions between the developed and developing worlds over fossil fuels and climate finance. The result is that it is now clear that global temperatures are set to overshoot the Paris-Agreement target of holding temperatures below 1.5 degrees centigrade above pre-industrial levels — at a time when global temperatures broke new heat records this year. The draft pact sought to call on countries to keep the overshoot as low and for as short-lived a period as possible, a considerable dilution from the original Paris-Agreement pledges, and suggested carbon-capture storage as a substitute for cutting emission. The latter in itself is controversial; it works for some industries but is limited as an economically scalable solution.

item.title: EU, Russia and Arab states derail COP31 talks over fuel and climate finance
item.description: The UN climate summit in Antalya ended without a consensus decision as countries clashed over fossil fuel phaseouts and climate finance, marking only the third such failure since 1995 ...
item.dc:creator: S Dinakar
item.content:encoded: In the end, COP31 — a nearly two-week-long, UN-led global climate summit of around 200 nations — in Antalya, Turkey, proved a cop-out. Running into record extra time, nations failed to agree on a cover decision, a political but non-binding statement on the causes of and solutions to climate change and the provision of climate finance, for only the third time since the summit was first held in 1995.
